title: EPA 608 Type III practice test
description: Free EPA Section 608 Type III (low-pressure appliances) practice questions. Every answer is explained and linked to the section of 40 CFR Part 82 it comes from.

questions.question: The rule on pressurizing low-pressure appliances sorts refrigerants by whether they boil at or below 85 °F. At what pressure is that boiling point taken?

options.A: 29.9 inches of mercury (standard atmospheric pressure)
options.B: 45 psia
options.C: 25 mm Hg absolute
options.D: 355 psia

questions.explanation: The rule refers to refrigerants "with boiling points at or below 85 degrees Fahrenheit at 29.9 inches of mercury (standard atmospheric pressure)." The 45 and 355 psia figures come from the pressure-class definitions, and 25 mm Hg absolute is the Table 1 level for low-pressure appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A chiller uses a refrigerant with a liquid phase saturation pressure of 15 psia at 104 °F. Which technician certification type does 40 CFR 82.161 require to service it?

options.A: Type I
options.B: Type II
options.C: Type III
options.D: None, because chillers are exempt

questions.explanation: A pressure "below 45 psia at 104 °F" makes this a low-pressure appliance, and persons who service low-pressure appliances "must be certified as Type III technicians." Type II covers medium-, high- and very high-pressure appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician will service small appliances, high-pressure rooftop units and low-pressure chillers. Which certification does 40 CFR 82.161 require for someone who works on all of these appliance types?

options.A: Type III
options.B: Type I
options.C: Type II
options.D: Universal

questions.explanation: Persons who work on all appliances described in paragraph (a)(1)(i) through (iii) "must be certified as Universal technicians." Type I, II or III alone covers only one of those appliance groups.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How is the low-pressure appliance row of Table 1 in 40 CFR 82.156 stated differently from the other rows?

options.A: It changes with charge size above 200 pounds
options.B: It applies only to recovery equipment made before November 15, 1993
options.C: It sets no required level at all
options.D: Its level is given as an absolute pressure in mm Hg rather than in inches of Hg vacuum

questions.explanation: The other rows give inches of Hg vacuum, while the table lists "Low-pressure appliance" at "25 mm Hg absolute" in both equipment columns. The row has no charge-size split and applies to equipment of either age.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An owner suspends the leak repair deadlines on a chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) by mothballing it. What must the owner's records document?

options.A: Daily temperature readings while it is shut down
options.B: The name of the EPA official who approved the mothballing
options.C: When the appliance was mothballed and when additional refrigerant was added to it
options.D: Only the date the appliance is finally retired

questions.explanation: Owners or operators who suspend deadlines by mothballing "must keep records documenting when the appliance was mothballed and when additional refrigerant was added to the appliance (or isolated component)." No EPA approval or daily readings are called for.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For a repair that is not major, with no evacuation to the atmosphere afterward, how does the requirement for a low-pressure appliance differ from the one for a high-pressure appliance?

options.A: The low-pressure appliance must be evacuated to 25 mm Hg absolute instead
options.B: The low-pressure appliance has no pressure requirement
options.C: The low-pressure appliance is pressurized to no higher than 0 psig, while the high-pressure appliance is evacuated to no higher than 0 psig
options.D: The low-pressure appliance is pressurized to 5 psig

questions.explanation: A medium-, high- or very high-pressure appliance must "Be evacuated to a pressure no higher than 0 psig," while a low-pressure appliance must "Be pressurized to a pressure no higher than 0 psig before it is opened." Both share the same 0 psig ceiling, reached from opposite directions.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A low-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant that boils at or below 85 °F at 29.9 inches of mercury. It needs a repair that is not major (and not an oil change), and it will not be evacuated to the atmosphere afterward. When pressurizing it before it is opened, what does the rule prohibit?

options.A: Using heat to raise the internal pressure
options.B: Using methods such as nitrogen that require subsequent purging
options.C: Covering openings when isolation is not possible
options.D: Raising the internal pressure to 0 psig

questions.explanation: For these refrigerants, persons "must not use methods such as nitrogen that require subsequent purging." The rule does not forbid heat, it requires covering openings when isolation is not possible, and 0 psig is the required pressure limit, not a prohibited one.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A low-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant that boils above 85 °F at 29.9 inches of mercury. After heat has raised its internal pressure as much as possible, up to what pressure may nitrogen be used before the appliance is opened for a non-major repair?

options.A: Atmospheric pressure
options.B: 10 psig
options.C: 25 psig
options.D: 5 psig

questions.explanation: For these refrigerants, persons must use heat first, "but may use nitrogen to raise the internal pressure of the appliance from the level attainable through use of heat to atmospheric pressure." Nitrogen may not push the pressure above atmospheric.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A low-pressure appliance needs a repair that is not major (and not an oil change), and it will not be evacuated to the atmosphere afterward. While pressurizing it, the technician finds that the part cannot be isolated. What does the rule require?

options.A: Notify EPA within 30 days
options.B: Add nitrogen to 5 psig
options.C: Cover openings
options.D: Replace the system receiver

questions.explanation: In the paragraph on pressurizing low-pressure appliances, the rule states: "Persons must cover openings when isolation is not possible." Nothing in that paragraph calls for adding nitrogen to 5 psig, notifying EPA, or replacing a receiver.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The oil-change provision lets oil be drained into a system receiver. How does the rule define a system receiver?

options.A: The isolated portion of the appliance, or a specific vessel within it, used to hold the refrigerant charge during servicing or repair
options.B: A purge unit mounted on a chiller
options.C: A recovery cylinder outside the appliance
options.D: A container for used oil sent to a reclaimer

questions.explanation: System receiver means "the isolated portion of the appliance, or a specific vessel within the appliance, that is used to hold the refrigerant charge during the servicing or repair of that appliance." It is part of the appliance, not an external cylinder or oil container.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A manufacturer sells a new low-pressure chiller charged with a non-exempt refrigerant. Under the prohibitions in 40 CFR 82.154, what must the chiller be equipped with so that refrigerant can be removed at servicing and disposal?

options.A: A process stub
options.B: A servicing aperture
options.C: A self-sealing valve
options.D: A one-time expansion device

questions.explanation: No one may sell or distribute an appliance, other than small appliances and appliances containing only exempt refrigerants, "unless it is equipped with a servicing aperture to facilitate the removal of refrigerant at servicing and disposal." The process stub requirement is for small appliances, and a self-sealing valve is a fitting on refrigerant containers.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Leaks in a chiller make the Table 1 level unattainable. What is the first step 40 CFR 82.156(a)(2) lists for the person opening or disposing of it?

options.A: Add nitrogen to the leaking components
options.B: Evacuate the whole chiller to 0 psig only
options.C: Isolate leaking from non-leaking components wherever possible
options.D: Notify EPA before opening the chiller

questions.explanation: The first step is: "Isolate leaking from non-leaking components wherever possible." Non-leaking components then go to the Table 1 levels, and leaking ones to the lowest level attainable without substantially contaminating the refrigerant.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the evacuation rule, who must verify that the required evacuation level has been reached, and when?

options.A: The owner, within 30 days after the repair
options.B: The technician, before the appliance or part is opened
options.C: EPA, during an inspection
options.D: The recovery equipment manufacturer, when the machine is certified

questions.explanation: The rule says "A technician must verify that the applicable level of evacuation has been reached" in the appliance or part before it is opened. The duty falls on the technician at the time of the job, not on the owner, EPA, or the equipment maker.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The table of maximum contaminant levels for equipment advertised as recycling equipment has a column for low-pressure (R-11, R-123, R-113) systems. Which contaminant is listed as not applicable (N/A) for those systems?

options.A: Particulates
options.B: Moisture
options.C: Acid content
options.D: Noncondensable gas

questions.explanation: The "MAXIMUM LEVELS OF CONTAMINANTS PERMISSIBLE IN REFRIGERANT PROCESSED" table shows N/A for noncondensable gas in the "Low-pressure (R-11, R-123, R-113)" column, with 2.0% for the other columns. Moisture, acid content and particulates all have listed limits for low-pressure systems.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An ice rink is cooled by a low-pressure chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant. Which category in the definitions does the ice rink appliance belong to for leak repair purposes?

options.A: Commercial refrigeration
options.B: Industrial process refrigeration
options.C: Comfort cooling
options.D: Small appliance

questions.explanation: The industrial process refrigeration definition states: "This sector also includes industrial ice machines, appliances used directly in the generation of electricity, and ice rinks." Commercial refrigeration covers retail food and cold storage, and comfort cooling covers occupied buildings.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the rolling average method in the leak rate definition, step 1 adds up the refrigerant added to the appliance over what period?

options.A: The previous 365-day period, or the shorter period since the last successful follow-up verification test showing all identified leaks were repaired
options.B: The time since the appliance was installed
options.C: The current calendar month
options.D: The last 30 days

questions.explanation: Step 1 takes "the sum of the pounds of refrigerant added to the appliance over the previous 365-day period (or over the period that has passed since the last successful follow-up verification test showing all identified leaks in the appliance were repaired, if that period is less than one year)." The sum is then divided by the full charge and multiplied by 100.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) is sending EPA a request for more time to complete leak repairs. The request contains no confidential business information. How must it be submitted?

options.A: By fax to the state environmental agency
options.B: Only by certified mail to the nearest EPA Regional Office
options.C: Electronically to 608reports@epa.gov
options.D: Through the technician's certifying program

questions.explanation: The rule says "All notifications must be submitted electronically to 608reports@epa.gov unless the notification contains confidential business information." Notifications with confidential business information go by mail to the Section 608 Program Manager at EPA headquarters, not to a Regional Office, a state agency or a certifying program.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A chiller owner (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) asks EPA for more than 30 days to finish leak repairs. Which item must the extension request include?

options.A: A letter of support from the chiller manufacturer
options.B: Copies of the technicians' certification cards
options.C: The reasons why more than 30 days are needed to complete the repair
options.D: A photograph of each leak

questions.explanation: Extension requests must include, among other items, "the reasons why more than 30 days (or 120 days if an industrial process shutdown is required) are needed to complete the repair." Manufacturer letters, certification cards and photographs are not on the list.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A building owner monitors a chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) with an automatic leak detection system instead of conducting annual leak inspections. Which records must the owner keep about the system?

options.A: Records of its installation and annual audit and calibration, each date it identified a leak, and the location of the leak
options.B: A monthly printout countersigned by EPA
options.C: None, because the system replaces leak inspections
options.D: Only the purchase receipt for the system

questions.explanation: If using an automatic leak detection system, the owner or operator "must maintain records regarding the installation and the annual audit and calibration of the system, a record of each date the monitoring system identified a leak, and the location of the leak." Using the system in place of inspections does not remove this recordkeeping duty.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A contractor's technician adds refrigerant to a hospital's chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant). Under the recordkeeping rule, which information must the record that the technician gives the hospital contain?

options.A: The technician's home address and date of birth
options.B: The chiller's purchase price and warranty number
options.C: The date of the service, the parts serviced, the type of service, the technician's name, and the amount and type of refrigerant added
options.D: A photograph of the gauges at the end of the job

questions.explanation: When the service is done by someone other than the owner or operator, "that person must provide a record containing the following information," which includes the date, the parts serviced, the type of service, "The name of the person performing the maintenance, service, repair, or disposal" and "The amount and type of refrigerant added to" the appliance. Prices, personal details and photographs are not on the list.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A comfort cooling chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant has exceeded its applicable leak rate. Unless an automatic leak detection system is used, what leak inspection schedule does 40 CFR 82.157 set for it?

options.A: Once every three months
options.B: Once per calendar year
options.C: Once every five years
options.D: Once every two years

questions.explanation: For comfort cooling appliances, leak inspections "must be conducted once per calendar year" until the owner shows the appliance has not leaked above the applicable rate for one year. Inspections every three months apply to commercial and industrial process refrigeration appliances of 500 pounds or more.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) writes a plan to retrofit it to a different refrigerant. Besides identifying the appliance and its location, which item must the plan contain?

options.A: The name of the wholesaler that will supply the new refrigerant
options.B: Copies of the certification cards of the technicians who will do the work
options.C: An itemized procedure for converting the appliance, including changes required for compatibility with the new substitute
options.D: Written approval from the chiller manufacturer

questions.explanation: A retrofit or retirement plan must contain, at a minimum, an "Itemized procedure for converting the appliance to a different refrigerant, including changes required for compatibility with the new substitute, if retrofitted." The rule's list does not include a supplier's name, technicians' cards or manufacturer approval.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A federal agency owns a comfort cooling chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) that it must retire under a plan. Because of the agency's procurement process, the quoted delivery time for the replacement is more than 30 weeks from the start of official procurement. How much time beyond the one-year plan period may the agency request?

options.A: Up to three additional years in a single request
options.B: Up to five additional years in a single request
options.C: Unlimited time, with no request needed
options.D: An additional year

questions.explanation: Owners or operators of federally owned commercial or comfort-cooling equipment "may request an additional year beyond the one-year period in paragraph (h) of this section" when a delivery time of more than 30 weeks "from the beginning of the official procurement process is quoted." Any further time needs a new request made before the end of the ninth month of that one-year extension.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an appliance with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant, purged refrigerant is left out of the annual leak rate only if it is destroyed at what verifiable destruction efficiency?

options.A: 98 percent or greater
options.B: 90 percent or greater
options.C: 80 percent or greater
options.D: 75 percent or greater

questions.explanation: Purged refrigerant "destroyed at a verifiable destruction efficiency of 98 percent or greater" is not counted toward the leak rate (paragraph (k)). Owners who use this exclusion must also keep monitoring records (paragraph (l)(9)) and notify EPA within 60 days after the facility first uses it (paragraph (m)(5)).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under §82.158(d), if recovery or recycling equipment certified by an approved equipment testing organization has a noncondensables purge device, what is the most refrigerant it may release through purging?

options.A: 3 percent of the refrigerant being recycled
options.B: 1 percent of the refrigerant being recycled
options.C: 5 percent of the refrigerant being recycled
options.D: 10 percent of the refrigerant being recycled

questions.explanation: The equipment standard says such equipment "must not release more than 3 percent" of the refrigerant being recycled through noncondensables purging. This is measured under the conditions of the applicable test appendix (B1, B2, B3, or B4).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A manufacturer builds a new recovery machine in 2025 for low-pressure chillers that use a non-flammable refrigerant. To be certified, the machine must be shown to reach the Table 2 evacuation level under the conditions of which appendix?

options.A: Appendix B1, based on ARI Standard 740-1993
options.B: Appendix B3, based on AHRI Standard 740-2016
options.C: Appendix B2, based on ARI Standard 740-1995
options.D: Appendix C, the test method for small appliances

questions.explanation: Equipment made or imported on or after January 1, 2017, must be certified as "capable of achieving the level of evacuation specified in Table 2 of this section under the conditions of appendix B3 (for non-flammable refrigerants) based upon AHRI Standard 740-2016." Appendices B1 and B2 apply to older equipment, and appendix C is for small-appliance recovery devices.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Before opening a low-pressure appliance (when none of the rule's exceptions apply), what must the technician evacuate to the Table 1 level?

options.A: The refrigerant, including all the liquid refrigerant
options.B: Only the refrigerant vapor
options.C: Only the refrigerant held in the compressor
options.D: Only the refrigerant held in the purge unit

questions.explanation: Technicians "must evacuate the refrigerant, including all the liquid refrigerant, to the levels in Table 1" using certified recovery and/or recycling equipment. Removing only the vapor, or only one component's refrigerant, leaves liquid behind and does not meet the rule.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A low-pressure chiller has a full charge of 400 pounds of refrigerant. Under what condition may system-dependent recovery equipment be used on it?

options.A: When a certified Type III technician supervises the recovery
options.B: When the recovery equipment was made before November 15, 1993
options.C: When the refrigerant will be returned to the same chiller
options.D: When the system-dependent equipment is permanently attached to the chiller as a pump-out unit

questions.explanation: System-dependent equipment "may not be used with appliances with a full charge of more than 15 pounds of refrigerant, unless the system-dependent equipment is permanently attached to the appliance as a pump-out unit." Supervision, equipment age, and where the refrigerant goes do not lift this limit.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An approved equipment testing organization certifies a recovery machine for chillers under 40 CFR 82.158(d). Besides low-loss fittings on all hoses and the limit on noncondensables purging, what must be measured under the applicable test appendix?

options.A: The machine's weight and noise level
options.B: Its liquid recovery rate and its vapor recovery rate, unless it has no inherent liquid or vapor recovery rate
options.C: The number of hours it can run before an oil change
options.D: The purity of the refrigerant after reclamation to appendix A

questions.explanation: The rule states: "The equipment must have its liquid recovery rate and its vapor recovery rate measured under the conditions of appendix B1, B2, B3, or B4 as applicable, unless the equipment has no inherent liquid or vapor recovery rate." Reprocessing to appendix A is a reclaimer's job, not a recovery-equipment test.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.158, Standards for recovery and/or recycling equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Low-pressure chillers must be evacuated to the Table 1 level before disposal. Someone cuts the refrigerant lines on an abandoned low-pressure chiller to steal copper, releasing refrigerant. How does the definition of disposal treat this act?

options.A: As disposal, because the definition includes vandalism of any appliance such that the refrigerant is released into the environment
options.B: As outside the disposal definition, because no technician was involved
options.C: As a de minimis release
options.D: As a seasonal variance

questions.explanation: Disposal means the process leading to and including, among other things, "The vandalism of any appliance such that the refrigerant is released into the environment or would be released into the environment if it had not been recovered prior to the destructive activity." A de minimis release is one tied to good faith attempts to recycle or recover refrigerant, and a seasonal variance is a removal and re-addition due to a change in season.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician performs a follow-up verification test on a repaired leak in a chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant. What must the technician do when the service is finished?

options.A: Give the owner or operator documentation of the test that meets the recordkeeping requirements
options.B: Send the test results to EPA within 30 days
options.C: Keep the only copy of the results at the technician's place of business
options.D: Nothing; verification test records are the owner's job alone

questions.explanation: Technicians conducting initial or follow-up verification tests "must, upon conclusion of that service, provide the owner or operator of the appliance with documentation that meets these requirements" (location, dates, repaired leaks tested, test types, and results). The rule does not call for sending the results to EPA.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An industrial process refrigeration chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant is leaking above its applicable rate when refrigerant is added. The repair requires an industrial process shutdown. Without any extension, how long does the owner have to identify and repair the leaks?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 120 days
options.C: 180 days
options.D: 270 days

questions.explanation: Leaks must be identified and repaired "within 30 days (or 120 days if an industrial process shutdown is required)." Because a shutdown is required, the 120-day period applies; 180 and 270 days are only outer limits of the extension for unavailable parts.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of an industrial process refrigeration appliance with a full charge of 800 pounds of a class II refrigerant wants to replace its quarterly leak inspections with an automatic leak detection system that directly detects refrigerant in air. Which components may such a system be used to monitor?

options.A: Only components located outdoors
options.B: Only components located inside an enclosed building or structure
options.C: Only components more than two meters above a support surface
options.D: Any component, indoors or outdoors, as long as the sensors detect 1,000 parts per million

questions.explanation: A system that directly detects refrigerant in air must "Only be used to monitor components located inside an enclosed building or structure," must accurately detect 10 parts per million and must alert at 100 parts per million. Quarterly inspections are waived only for portions continuously monitored by a system that "is audited or calibrated annually."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A new chiller uses R-245fa. How do the Section 608 definitions class this appliance?

options.A: As a medium-pressure appliance
options.B: As a high-pressure appliance
options.C: As a very high-pressure appliance
options.D: As a low-pressure appliance, because the definition names appliances using R-245fa as an example

questions.explanation: A low-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant "with a liquid phase saturation pressure below 45 psia at 104 °F," and the definition adds: "Examples include but are not limited to appliances using R-11, R-123, R-113, and R-245fa." None of the other pressure-class definitions names R-245fa.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: After writing a retrofit or retirement plan, the owner of a chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) wants EPA to relieve it of the obligation to retrofit or retire the chiller. What must the owner establish and agree to?

options.A: Within 180 days of the plan's date, that the chiller no longer exceeds the applicable leak rate, and agree in writing to repair all identified leaks within one year of the plan's date
options.B: That the chiller has run for 30 days since the plan's date; no repair commitment is needed
options.C: That the chiller's refrigerant has been reclaimed, at any time before the plan's schedule ends
options.D: Nothing; relief is not available once a plan has been written

questions.explanation: The owner or operator may request relief "if the owner or operator can establish within 180 days of the plan's date that the appliance no longer exceeds the applicable leak rate and if the owner or operator agrees in writing to repair all identified leaks within one year of the plan's date." The request is considered approved unless EPA says otherwise within 60 days.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) leaves refrigerant added for a seasonal variance out of its leak rate calculation. What must the owner's records show?

options.A: EPA's written approval for each seasonal addition
options.B: That the owner is using the seasonal variance flexibility, and the amounts added and removed
options.C: Nothing, because seasonal additions are excluded from the calculation
options.D: The outdoor temperature on each day the chiller ran

questions.explanation: Owners or operators that exclude seasonal variance additions "must maintain records stating that they are using the seasonal variance flexibility and documenting the amount added and removed." Leaving the addition out of the calculation does not excuse these records.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A facility has several chillers subject to the leak repair requirements. What does the leak rate definition require about the calculation method?

options.A: Comfort cooling appliances must use one method and industrial process refrigeration another
options.B: Each appliance must use a different method
options.C: The technician may switch methods at each refrigerant addition
options.D: The same method must be used for all appliances subject to the leak repair requirements at the facility

questions.explanation: The definition states: "The same method must be used for all appliances subject to the leak repair requirements located at an operating facility." Switching methods between appliances or between additions is not allowed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the federal definition, how is an appliance's leak rate expressed?

options.A: As pounds of refrigerant lost per month
options.B: As the percentage of the full charge lost since the appliance was installed
options.C: As the percentage of the full charge that would be lost over a 12-month period if the current rate of loss continued
options.D: As the percentage of the full charge lost over the last 30 days

questions.explanation: The leak rate is "the percentage of the appliance's full charge that would be lost over a 12-month period if the current rate of loss were to continue over that period." It is a percentage of full charge projected over 12 months, not pounds or a loss since installation.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An industrial process refrigeration appliance (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) is being retrofitted under a plan. The custom-built replacement component has a quoted delivery time of more than 30 weeks, and the owner requests more time on that basis. After the parts arrive, how long does the owner have to install them?

options.A: No set deadline; the parts may be installed whenever convenient
options.B: 18 months
options.C: 180 days
options.D: 120 days

questions.explanation: The custom-built extension applies when the supplier "has quoted a delivery time of more than 30 weeks from when the order is placed," and "The appliance or appliance components must be installed within 120 days after receiving delivery of the necessary parts." The 180-day figure is an outer limit on leak repair time for unavailable components, and 18 months is the automatic retirement extension for exempt-substitute replacements.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A comfort cooling chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) exceeds its leak rate. No industrial process shutdown is involved, and local regulations make a repair within 30 days impossible. By when must the owner request the extension from EPA?

options.A: Within 180 days of the appliance exceeding the leak rate
options.B: Within 30 days of the appliance exceeding the applicable leak rate
options.C: By March 1 of the following year
options.D: Within seven months of discovering the leak

questions.explanation: The owner or operator "must request an extension from EPA at the address specified in paragraph (m) of this section within 30 days (or 120 days if an industrial process shutdown is required) of the appliance exceeding the applicable leak rate." Seven months is the deadline for asking for more than one year to retrofit or retire, and 180 days is an outer limit on repair time for unavailable components.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant requests more time for leak repairs under §82.157(f). How is the request treated?

options.A: It must first be approved at a public hearing
options.B: It takes effect only after EPA sends written approval
options.C: It is considered approved unless EPA notifies the owner or operator otherwise
options.D: It is available only to federally owned appliances

questions.explanation: For repair deadline extensions, "The request will be considered approved unless EPA notifies the owners or operators otherwise." No written approval or hearing is needed, and the extension is not limited to federal equipment.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant leaks above its applicable rate, and the owner intends to retire it rather than repair the leak. By when must a retrofit or retirement plan be created?

options.A: Within one year of the leak
options.B: Within seven months of discovering the leak
options.C: By March 1 of the following year
options.D: Within 30 days of the appliance leaking above the applicable leak rate

questions.explanation: The owner or operator "must create a retrofit or retirement plan within 30 days of" the appliance leaking above the applicable rate when it intends to retrofit or retire rather than repair. Seven months is the deadline for asking EPA for more than one year to finish the work, not for creating the plan.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an appliance with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant, which requirement applies to a retrofit or retirement plan?

options.A: It must be signed by an authorized company official, dated, and accessible at the site of the appliance
options.B: It must be filed with the state environmental agency
options.C: It must be signed by a Type III technician and mailed to the appliance manufacturer
options.D: It must be posted publicly online

questions.explanation: The plan "must be signed by an authorized company official, dated, accessible at the site of the appliance" in paper or electronic form and available for EPA inspection on request. The rule does not call for a technician's signature, state filing, or public posting.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a comfort cooling chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant will retire it and replace it with an appliance using a substitute refrigerant exempted under §82.154(a). How long is the owner automatically allowed to retire the chiller?

options.A: 18 months
options.B: 13 months
options.C: One year
options.D: 30 weeks

questions.explanation: Owners or operators "are automatically allowed 18 months to retire an appliance if the replacement appliance uses a substitute refrigerant exempted under § 82.154(a)." One year (and at most 13 months) is the normal limit when this extension does not apply.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an appliance with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant, which item must the leak inspection records include?

options.A: The technician's Social Security number
options.B: A photograph of each leak
options.C: The signature of an EPA inspector
options.D: A certification that all visible and accessible parts of the appliance were inspected

questions.explanation: Leak inspection records must include the date, the method(s) used, the location of each leak found, and "a certification that all visible and accessible parts of the appliance were inspected." Photographs, an EPA signature, or a Social Security number are not listed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant will retrofit it to a different refrigerant under a retrofit or retirement plan. What must happen to the leaks that have been identified?

options.A: They may be left as they are, because the refrigerant is being changed
options.B: All identified leaks must be repaired as part of the retrofit
options.C: They must be reported to EPA instead of repaired
options.D: Only leaks larger than the applicable leak rate must be repaired

questions.explanation: The rule states: "All identified leaks must be repaired as part of any retrofit under such a plan." Changing the refrigerant does not remove the duty to fix the leaks found.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a comfort cooling chiller with a full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant uses a repair deadline extension because one part is on back order. Other leaks that significantly contribute to the leak rate can be fixed without extra time. When must those repairs be completed and verified?

options.A: Within the initial 30-day repair period
options.B: Within 30 days of receiving the back-ordered part
options.C: Within 180 days of the appliance exceeding the leak rate
options.D: Before the next annual leak inspection

questions.explanation: Repairs to leaks that significantly contribute to the exceedance "and that do not require additional time must be completed and verified within the initial 30 day repair period" (120 days if an industrial process shutdown is required). The extra time covers only the repair that needs the missing part.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A proctored Type III test session has just ended. What does Appendix D require the proctors to do with the test forms, answer sheets, scratch paper and notes?

options.A: Hand the scratch paper back to the applicants
options.B: Leave the answer sheets with the applicants until results are issued
options.C: Shred them at the test site
options.D: Collect all of them and place them in a sealed envelope

questions.explanation: Appendix D states: "After the completion of a test, proctors must collect all test forms, answer sheets, scratch paper and notes. These items are to be placed in a sealed envelope." Returning or destroying the materials at the site does not meet this rule.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A low-pressure chiller with no leaks needs a repair that is not major. After the repair is finished, the chiller will be evacuated to the atmosphere. What does 40 CFR 82.156(a) require before the chiller is opened?

options.A: Pressurize it to no higher than 0 psig, using heat and then nitrogen if needed
options.B: Pressurize it to no higher than 5 psig
options.C: Evacuate the refrigerant, including all the liquid refrigerant, to the Table 1 level of 25 mm Hg absolute
options.D: Cover the openings and open it at its current pressure

questions.explanation: The 0 psig pressurizing option applies only "If evacuation of the appliance to the atmosphere is not to be performed after completion of the maintenance, service, or repair" and the work is not major. Otherwise technicians "must evacuate the refrigerant, including all the liquid refrigerant, to the levels in Table 1", which lists "25 mm Hg absolute" for a low-pressure appliance.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A shop owns two certified recovery machines, one manufactured in 1992 and one in 2018. A low-pressure chiller with no leaks will be opened for a major repair. How do the Table 1 evacuation levels for the two machines compare?

options.A: The 1992 machine has a less strict level, as in the medium-pressure rows
options.B: Only the 2018 machine may be used, because Table 1 sets no level for older equipment
options.C: Both machines must reach the same level, 25 mm Hg absolute
options.D: The 1992 machine needs to reach only 0 inches of Hg vacuum

questions.explanation: Table 1 lists "Low-pressure appliance" at "25 mm Hg absolute" in both columns, for equipment made before and for equipment made on or after November 15, 1993. Only the medium- and some high-pressure rows set a less strict level for older equipment.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.156, Proper evacuation of refrigerant from appliances (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a comfort cooling low-pressure chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) will retire it under a retrofit or retirement plan. Besides identifying the chiller and its location and giving the type and full charge of its refrigerant, which items must the plan contain?

options.A: The names of every technician who has serviced the chiller
options.B: A plan for the disposition of the recovered refrigerant and a plan for the disposition of the chiller
options.C: The purchase price of the replacement appliance
options.D: Proof that the replacement appliance has already been ordered

questions.explanation: A retrofit or retirement plan must, at a minimum, include a "Plan for the disposition of recovered refrigerant" and a "Plan for the disposition of the appliance, if retired", along with a schedule for completion.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A comfort cooling low-pressure chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) leaks above its applicable leak rate. It is located in an area subject to radiological contamination, no parts are on back order, and the owner meets the other extension requirements of 40 CFR 82.157(f). How much additional time for the repair does the rule permit?

options.A: Up to 30 days after receiving delivery of the necessary components, not to exceed 180 days
options.B: Exactly one additional year
options.C: The extent needed to conduct and finish repairs in a safe working environment
options.D: None, because the repair period for this chiller is fixed at 30 days

questions.explanation: Where "The appliance is located in an area subject to radiological contamination", "Additional time is permitted to the extent needed to conduct and finish repairs in a safe working environment." The 180-day cap belongs to the condition where components are not available.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The owner of a comfort cooling low-pressure chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) has asked EPA for more time to finish leak repairs under 40 CFR 82.157(f). Later the owner learns that the estimated completion date given in the request must be extended. What does the rule require?

options.A: Submit to EPA a new estimated date of completion and documentation of the reason for the change, within 30 days of identifying that the date must be extended
options.B: Withdraw the request and start a new 30-day repair period
options.C: Nothing further, because the original request is considered approved unless EPA objects
options.D: Submit a new estimate only if EPA asks for one

questions.explanation: "If the estimated completion date is to be extended, a new estimated date of completion and documentation of the reason for that change must be submitted to EPA within 30 days of identifying that the completion date must be extended."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An industrial process refrigeration low-pressure chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) is under a retrofit plan, and state regulations make finishing the retrofit within one year impossible. The owner will ask EPA for more than one year. What submission deadline does 40 CFR 82.157(i) set for the request?

options.A: Within one year of the plan's date
options.B: Within 13 months of when the plan was required
options.C: Within seven months of discovering the appliance exceeded the applicable leak rate
options.D: Within 18 months of discovering the appliance exceeded the applicable leak rate

questions.explanation: The extension request "must be submitted to EPA at the address specified in § 82.157(m) within seven months of discovering the appliance exceeded the applicable leak rate."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An owner leaves purged refrigerant that is destroyed out of the annual leak rate calculation for a low-pressure chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant). Which data must the supporting records include?

options.A: Only the total pounds of refrigerant purchased each year
options.B: The names of all technicians who serviced the purge unit
options.C: The chiller's original installation date
options.D: Flow rate, quantity or concentration of the refrigerant in the vent stream, and periods of purge flow

questions.explanation: Records must be based on a reliable monitoring strategy, and "Records must include flow rate, quantity or concentration of the refrigerant in the vent stream, and periods of purge flow."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A facility excludes destroyed purged refrigerant from the annual leak rate calculation of its low-pressure chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) for the first time. What notification deadline does 40 CFR 82.157(m)(5) set?

options.A: Within 120 days after the first time the exclusion is used by the facility
options.B: Within one year after the first time the exclusion is used by the facility
options.C: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which the exclusion is first used
options.D: Within 60 days after the first time the exclusion is used by the facility

questions.explanation: Owners or operators "must notify EPA at this address within 60 days after the first time the exclusion is used by the facility where the appliance is located." The report must include the information in paragraph (l)(9).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.157, Appliance maintenance and leak repair (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: After a leak on a low-pressure chiller (full charge of 50 or more pounds of a class I or class II refrigerant) is repaired, the technician plans to use fluorescent dye and black light for the follow-up verification test. How does the definition of follow-up verification test treat this method?

options.A: It may be used only on small appliances
options.B: It is one of the potential methods the definition lists
options.C: It must be carried out by an approved equipment testing organization
options.D: It is allowed only after a sight glass check

questions.explanation: "Potential methods for follow-up verification tests include, but are not limited to, the use of soap bubbles as appropriate, electronic or ultrasonic leak detectors, pressure or vacuum tests, fluorescent dye and black light, infrared or near infrared tests, and handheld gas detection devices."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician wants Type III certification. What kind of test does Appendix D require the technician to pass?

options.A: A hands-on recovery demonstration on a low-pressure chiller
options.B: An on-site or mail-in test, in whichever format the certifying program chooses
options.C: An open-book test taken online without a proctor
options.D: A closed-book, proctored test, administered in a secure environment by an EPA-approved certifying program

questions.explanation: "Technicians must pass a closed-book, proctored test, administered in a secure environment, by an EPA-approved certifying program to be certified as a Type II or Type III technician." The choice of an on-site or mail-in format is given only to organizations providing Type I certification only.
